content:
The Time, Speed & Distance chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Time, Speed & Distance tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Time, Speed & Distance

Speed–distance–time, relative speed, trains, boats and streams, races and average speed.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Speed = Distance/Time; x km/h = x·5/18 m/s.
  • Two equal distances at u and v: average = 2uv/(u+v) (harmonic mean).
  • Relative speed = u−v (same direction), u+v (opposite).
  • Boat: downstream b+s, upstream b−s.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Taking the simple mean of two speeds for equal distances (use the harmonic mean).
  • Forgetting to add the train’s own length when crossing a platform.
  • Sign errors in relative speed.

quiz.title: CAT Time, Speed & Distance Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A train running at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train in meters?
questions.explanation: Speed of train = 72 km/h = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Length of train = Speed * Time = 20 * 15 = 300 meters.

questions.q: A man can row downstream at 12 km/h and upstream at 8 km/h. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Speed of current = (Downstream speed - Upstream speed) / 2 = (12 - 8) / 2 = 4 / 2 = 2 km/h.

questions.q: A train 180 meters long is running at a speed of 54 km/h. How much time will it take to cross a platform that is 270 meters long?
questions.explanation: Speed of train = 54 km/h = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s. Total distance to cover = Length of train + Length of platform = 180 + 270 = 450 meters. Time = Distance / Speed = 450 / 15 = 30 seconds.

questions.q: The speed of a boat in still water is 14 km/h and the speed of the current is 4 km/h. What is the time taken by the boat to travel 36 km downstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = Speed in still water + Speed of current = 14 + 4 = 18 km/h. Time taken = Distance / Downstream speed = 36 / 18 = 2.0 hours.

questions.q: A traveler covers half of a total distance at 50 km/h and the other half at 75 km/h. What is the average speed of the traveler for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean: (2 * s1 * s2) / (s1 + s2) = (2 * 50 * 75) / (50 + 75) = 7500 / 125 = 60 km/h.

questions.q: A train 240 meters long passes a telegraph post in 16 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation: Speed in m/s = Length / Time = 240 / 16 = 15 m/s. Convert to km/h by multiplying by 18/5: 15 * (18/5) = 3 * 18 = 54 km/h.

questions.q: A boat can row upstream at 9 km/h and downstream at 15 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation: Speed in still water = (Downstream + Upstream) / 2 = (15 + 9) / 2 = 24 / 2 = 12 km/h.

questions.q: A train running at a speed of 90 km/h crosses a pole in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train in meters?
questions.explanation: Speed of train = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. Length of train = Speed * Time = 25 * 12 = 300 meters.

questions.q: A boat rows downstream at 16 km/h and upstream at 10 km/h. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Speed of the stream = (Downstream speed - Upstream speed) / 2 = (16 - 10) / 2 = 6 / 2 = 3 km/h.

questions.q: A train running at a speed of 54 km/h crosses a pole in 20 seconds. What is the length of the train in meters?
questions.explanation: Speed of train = 54 km/h = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s. Length of train = Speed * Time = 15 * 20 = 300 meters.

faq.q: What is the average speed for equal distances?
faq.a: The harmonic mean 2uv/(u+v), NOT the arithmetic mean.

faq.q: How long to cross a platform?
faq.a: Time = (train length + platform length)/speed; for a pole it is just train length/speed.
